works.title: Moth
works.capture: Massey University scan of a moth from its art collection, published in 2019. The thin antennae and legs are included. The exact creation date and dimensions are unrecorded.
works.evidence: Official university model identifies its collection and bronze medium. The publisher spells the artist surname Thompson; artist and gallery references identify the New Zealand moth sculptor as Elizabeth Thomson.

works.title: Data-Confluences 006: Africa
works.capture: Original digital sculpture published by Clarissa Ribeiro. Its form combines environmental recordings shared across continents, including a contribution by Ruy Cezar Campos from Sangano, Angola. This work was created digitally and has no fixed physical dimensions.
works.evidence: Artist’s primary model dates the series to 2021 and credits the Angola contributor. Artist website describes the project, created in Fortaleza, Brazil. Filed with the artist’s Brazilian practice rather than treating the title Africa as the work’s geographical origin.

works.title: La Précarité de la Paix
works.capture: Holospasm Studio capture of the public sculpture and pedestal. A person carrying a book and a weapon faces a threatening animal. Semise’s publication connects the work with the artist’s encounters with the Sahrawi people.
works.evidence: Commissioner’s 2007 publication dates the work and inauguration to 2003 and identifies patinated bronze and the address. This primary record takes precedence over 2001 in the scan title.

works.title: Sténos (maquette)
works.capture: Holospasm Studio scan of a maquette for Sténos, the monumental installation created for the 2019 Lyon Biennale. This is the preparatory sculpture, not a scan of the enlarged installation. Hands and mask-like faces form an assembled body.
works.evidence: Primary scan explicitly describes a maquette. The museum documents plaster maquettes made from wax casts of the artist’s hands, then scanned and enlarged; the finished installation entered macLYON. Do not attribute museum ownership or full installation dimensions to this maquette.

works.title: Shiva Nataraja (Lord of Dance)
works.artist: Sri Pradakaran, Sri Govindan and Sri Pratiban
works.museum: Birmingham Museum of Art, Collection of the Art Fund, Inc.
works.capture: Dolphin Multimedia capture of the 2013 bronze by Sri Pradakaran, Sri Govindan and Sri Pratiban at Shri Rajan Industries, Tamil Nadu. The contemporary casting continues the lost-wax tradition of southern India. The base and a small area of the sculpture garden are included.
works.evidence: Museum collection record and 2016 spotlight name all three makers, give the date, dimensions, bronze medium, foundry and accession. Contemporary manufacture is explicit in the museum’s documentation.
